item.text: I’ll inspect the workspace and the existing `starter.hip` shape first, then I’ll wire the kernel into that interface and compile if the local toolchain is available.
`rg` isn’t installed here, but the workspace is tiny: just `starter.hip`. I’m reading that now so the implementation matches the expected exported symbol and launch style.

The kernel naturally maps to independent 32-value groups. I’m going with a block that processes multiple groups, using shared memory for the 32-lane reductions and pair packing so the behavior is explicit and doesn’t depend on wavefront shuffle details.

I’m about to edit `starter.hip`. The core choices are: pair-thread packing (one thread handles the even/odd pair that becomes one byte), exact bit-based scale exponent computation, and explicit threshold comparisons for tie-to-even E2M1 rounding.
The first pass is in place. I’m doing a local syntax compile now; after that I’ll do a small CPU-side reference check if I can build a simple host harness against HIP.
`hipcc` is available, which is handy. I’m compiling for `gfx950` specifically so any target-specific issues show up before we call this done.

The syntax compile passed cleanly. I’m making one small performance-oriented refinement now: split FP16 and BF16 into separate template instantiations so the inner loop doesn’t carry a runtime dtype branch.

The templated version also compiles for `gfx950`. I’m going one step further with a tiny local HIP harness in `/tmp` to compare a few deterministic cases against a CPU reference, assuming this environment has a usable GPU runtime.
The small harness is in place under `/tmp` and uses its own CPU reference; it doesn’t touch or depend on any evaluator materials. I’m compiling and running it now.

The harness couldn’t actually launch a kernel here (`hipErrorInvalidValue`, likely no matching GPU runtime available), so I’m treating compile as the local verification signal. I’m also replacing the shared-memory reduction with 16-lane wave shuffles, which is a better fit for `gfx950` and avoids block barriers in the hot path.
The shuffle-based kernel compiles cleanly for `gfx950`. I’m doing one linked build with the harness as a final sanity check that the exported symbol and templated launch are linkable.

The linked build succeeded too; only the throwaway harness has warnings from ignoring HIP return values. I’m doing a last source pass now for any edge-case footguns around scale exponent, sign handling, and output bounds.

One more refinement from the edge-case pass: I’m changing the shuffle reduction to address lanes explicitly within the wave instead of relying on subgroup-width partition semantics. That keeps the fast path but makes the grouping behavior more obvious on wave64 hardware.
The explicit-lane shuffle version compiles as well. I’m checking the final diff now so I can give you a concise handoff with exactly what changed and what was verified.

item.text:
Implemented `aiter_rs_quant_mxfp4_even` in [starter.hip](/workspace/starter.hip:173).

What changed:
- Added HIP kernel for FP16 and BF16 paths.
- Computes MXFP4 scale bytes with the specified even-mode exponent rule.
- Quantizes to E2M1 with tie-to-even thresholds and sign-preserving negative zero.
- Packs even values into low nibbles and odd values into high nibbles.
- Uses 16 threads per 32-value group, vectorized 32-bit pair loads, and wave shuffle reduction for `amax`.

Verification:
- `hipcc --offload-arch=gfx950 -c starter.hip -o /tmp/starter.o` passes.
- Linked successfully with a small local harness.
- Could not run the harness meaningfully in this environment because the HIP runtime launch returned `hipErrorInvalidValue`, likely due to unavailable/mismatched GPU runtime here.
